subject: Food Science
title: Why Food Spoils
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Why Food Spoils.

hook.text: Fresh milk goes sour, bread goes moldy, meat turns green. Spoilage is microbes eating your food before you do.

buildup.text: Spoilage bacteria break down proteins, fats, and carbohydrates into foul-smelling compounds. The food becomes inedible.

discovery.text: Pseudomonas is the main spoiler of refrigerated meat and dairy. It grows even at 4°C, slowly but relentlessly.

twist.text: Spoiled food usually won't make you sick. Spoilage bacteria and pathogens are different organisms with different effects.

climax.text: Food that smells fine can harbor deadly pathogens. Food that smells terrible is often just unpleasant, not dangerous.

punchline.text: Your nose detects spoilage. It can't detect danger. Two different problems.

quiz.question: Is spoiled food always dangerous to eat?
options: No—spoilage bacteria usually differ from pathogens that cause illness
